content: Large-print books, also referred to as large-type or large-font books, are publications designed with significantly larger typefaces or fonts to accommodate individuals with impaired vision. These materials can be in physical, digital, or other formats, and their primary purpose is to enhance readability for those with visual challenges. Public libraries, particularly those catering to individuals with special needs, often include large-print versions of books in their collections. These are typically offered alongside other accessible formats, such as Braille editions. Among librarians, large print is generally defined as text that is at least 16 points in size. In some cases, the type inside these books is enlarged to approximately double the size of the original print. Historically, large-print books were produced with plain dust jackets that featured only text and were color-coded to indicate different genres. For example, black was used for mysteries, red for general fiction, blue for romances, and orange for westerns. While these editions fulfilled the needs of visually impaired readers, their oversized dimensions often made them cumbersome for elderly individuals with limited physical strength to handle. In 1969, a company called Ulverscroft, led by Thorpe, began reformatting books into 16-point type while maintaining standard-sized bindings. These books retained the color-coded plain dust jackets. This innovation significantly improved the acceptance of large-print books in public libraries. Thorpe himself became a prominent advocate for large-print books, traveling extensively across English-speaking countries to promote their acquisition for senior readers. Today, many publishers release large-print editions of certain books simultaneously with their regular print editions. These large-print versions often feature the same full-color dust jackets and designs as their standard counterparts. Most public libraries in English-speaking regions now have dedicated large-print sections, and many bookstores also stock a selection of large-print editions.
